meta.title: Europe — remarkable individual trees for accidental walking discovery

import.warning: The research evidence remains useful, but catalogue presence does not mean editorial approval. Do not re-import these rows.

meta.decision: Stopped below target rather than pad. Every included row passed the named living individual, public access/visibility, current status, exact coordinate, story and 19/25 score gates.
meta.score_contract: Minimum 19/25; story and walkability each at least 4/5.
meta.source_contract: Each include has European/national champion evidence plus a live map object, with a current land-manager source where map evidence alone was insufficient.
meta.access_contract: Specific individual only; public path, ticketed public garden, or safe public visibility. No school-only, private-garden-only, illegal reservoir-zone or unverified estate access.
meta.dedupe_contract: Normalised global aliases and global nearest-neighbour distance checked against live Map-2/data/spots.json at 120 m; internal candidates also checked at 120 m.
research_notes: Historic contest coordinates were not silently trusted: when a live named tree object disagreed, the dossier retains and explains the stronger current coordinate.
Major Oak was removed after a June 2026 death confirmation; upright deadwood is not a living category member.
Luras and Monte Barbeiro were removed because the available story was chiefly great age/size, explicitly outside this category contract.

An OSM object is a present-map corroboration, not the heritage authority; the Tree of the Year national organiser, municipal manager, museum, arboretum or other land manager supplies the authority signal.

geography_review.rule: Every retained tree now uses an honest municipality, metropolitan grouping or explicit physical region, lies inside the raw declared bbox and infers back to that same registry entry.
geography_review.validation: 45/45 retained tree rows are inside their raw declared bbox and infer to their explicit city or region.

included.s: the flood oak that held a house in place
included.q: The Guardian Oak of Višňová Dub ochránce ve Višňové 0353, Víska, Višňová Czech Republic
included.w: During the 2010 floods, this oak braced a half-timbered house long enough for a couple and their dog to escape onto its roof. Scarred but still standing beside the village road, it turns an ordinary walk through Víska into a close encounter with a piece of living civil defence.

access.evidence: Public roadside visibility in Víska; stay on the village road and outside the root zone.
access.safety_filter: No climbing, hollow entry, fence crossing or root-zone shortcuts; follow any local closure or land-manager instruction.

included.s: a forgotten First World War memorial found again
included.q: The Peace Tree Peace Tree, Woodvale Park Woodvale Park, Woodvale Road, Belfast Northern Ireland
included.w: Suffrage-era veterans planted this oak in 1919 for those who did not return from the First World War. Forgotten for decades, it was rediscovered in 2006 and restored as a civic memorial. Belfast City Council now explicitly lists the Peace Tree among the free park's walking attractions.

access.evidence: Free municipal park with several walking routes and published daily opening times.
